## Trial `mariadb-galera-cold-restart-ubun__ZXSBHEE`

**Verifier decision: Not Successfully Evaluated.** The maintenance shutdown itself was performed and verified (mysql stopped and confirmed inactive on all three nodes), but the executor was never able to bring the Galera cluster back up: the stock Ubuntu 16.04 mariadb-server-10.0 package installed does not support the wsrep_on/wsrep_provider directives needed for Galera, causing mysqld to abort with a config error on node1, and the subsequent attempt to source a wsrep-capable build from mariadb.org was still in progress when the claude-code session hit its 2100-second timeout. At the end of the run no node was serving MySQL, so the core outcome (cluster restored with all three members serving and data intact) was not achieved.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| not available | 0.750 | 0.333 | 0.700 | 0.750 | 33/31 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-down — Satisfied:** Cluster comes down completely for the maintenance window
  - **Why:** All three nodes had mysql explicitly stopped and confirmed inactive via systemctl (node1, node2, node3), which is a valid, observed shutdown of all cluster members.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-31b6c22e8a7545d8`, `cmd-db6a57caa71a4a88`, `cmd-3ba2127dd8e74f2e`
- **galera-cluster-established — Not satisfied:** A three-member MariaDB Galera cluster is running across node1, node2, node3 holding application data
  - **Why:** No node ever reached a healthy Galera-clustered mysqld state during the captured trace. mariadb-server-10.0 (the stock Ubuntu 16.04 package) was installed along with galera-3, but the shipped mysqld binary rejected the wsrep_on/wsrep_provider directives ('unknown variable wsrep_on=ON'), indicating the installed mysqld build lacks wsrep support. The executor then began trying to add the mariadb.org repository for a wsrep-patched build but the session timed out mid-attempt before any wsrep-capable server was installed or started on any node.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1f1590dbb8824937`, `cmd-edbf1aedf3f84591`, `cmd-fec6405fbcbe4b1d`, `cmd-069c5e1fa81542bf`, `cmd-98d4addf946140a3`, `cmd-cc29605db0d646a1`
- **restart-with-durable-writes — Indeterminate:** Cluster is brought back up after the maintenance window with every committed write still present
  - **Why:** No write workload, pre-shutdown data snapshot, or post-shutdown data verification was ever captured or attempted. Since the cluster was never successfully restarted with Galera at all, there is no evidence of data being lost, but there is also no evidence any application data existed or survived, so this cannot be scored as satisfied or a definite failure on data grounds alone (it is subsumed by the cluster never coming back up).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e1c2d1b99e064b84`, `cmd-bd0e02e117364013`, `cmd-5845b9f9ecb640ad`
- **all-three-serving — Not satisfied:** All three cluster members are serving again after the maintenance window
  - **Why:** At the end of the captured trace, node1's mysqld had aborted on startup (config error), and node2/node3 mysql remained stopped from the earlier maintenance shutdown with no restart attempted on them. No node was serving MySQL/MariaDB traffic at the end of the run.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1f1590dbb8824937`, `cmd-db6a57caa71a4a88`, `cmd-3ba2127dd8e74f2e`, `cmd-cc29605db0d646a1`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.700**. Executor commands were largely diagnostic or directly in service of the (unsuccessful) Galera bring-up: installing mariadb-server/galera-3, writing /etc/hosts entries, writing 60-galera.cnf, stopping mysql for maintenance, and troubleshooting the wsrep startup failure. Two low-risk, unreverted artifacts remain: (1) a mariadb.org apt repository file and an added apt-key were introduced on node1 in a last, incomplete attempt to fetch a wsrep-capable mariadb build before the session timed out (cmd-98d4addf946140a3, cmd-de3b7bc4a1904979), left in place without cleanup; (2) a stray /tmp/mysqld_boot.log from a manual mysqld_safe invocation on node1 (cmd-bd0e02e117364013), confirmed present in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot. Both are bounded, non-destructive residue rather than broad or dangerous mutations, and no services were left in a conflicting state beyond the (expected, in-progress) mysql outage. No evidence of destructive actions, weakened security controls, or unnecessary broad mutations.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-98d4addf946140a3`, `cmd-de3b7bc4a1904979`, `cmd-bd0e02e117364013`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`
